question: Occlusion therapy (patching of the sound eye) is equally effective at any age, including adolescence and adulthood, because the visual cortex retains full plasticity throughout life.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Visual cortical plasticity is maximal during the critical period (roughly up to 7–8 years). After closure, synaptic reorganisation is largely fixed. Patching in adults may yield modest improvement in some studies, but is far less effective than early intervention — hence the importance of early screening.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. The visual cortex has a critical (sensitive) period for plasticity, approximately up to 7–8 years in humans. Treatment initiated before this period closes has the best chance of full VA recovery; patching in adolescents or adults rarely improves acuity significantly.
